title: Mechanism of Hydrogen Atom Transfer on Water Surfaces from Nonanoic Acid to Molecular Photosensitizers
content: Photosensitized reactions at water plays an important role in atmospheric chemistry, but their microscopic mechanism are largely unknown. In this work, we explore computationally the photosensitized hydrogen-atom transfer reactions from nonanoic acid (NA) to the photo sensitizers 4-benzoylbenzoic acid (4BBA) and 4-imidazolecarboxaldehyde (4IC) in large water cluster. Excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations as the principal method used. The following main results are obtained, (i) The process occur preferentially at the air-water interface. Agreements with the experiments on the photo-excitation spectra is good, much better than for 4BBA-NA and 4IC-NA complexes computed in gas phase, (ii) Excited-state dynamics simulation shows ultrafsat hydrogen-atom transfer of the carboxylic O-H hydrogen of NA to the carbonyl oxygen of the photosensitizers for the lowest excited singlet state, (iii) No hydrogen-atom transfer is observed for the corresponding triplet trajectories. It is suggested that excited-state AIMD simulation for photosensitizer-reagent complex in large water cluster can be suitable for unraveling photosensitized reaction mechanism for other photosensitizers.
